note: Committed, reviewed design input (LampaGJ/swu-mcp#25), versioned like complementarity.json. threats: a threat fires on an archetype when the sum of its profile metrics (mean copies per deck, or the named ratio) is at least min and at most max; thresholds sit near the 75th percentile of the 40 largest tournament archetypes of the 2026-07-20..2026-10-17 window (meanCost near the 25th). relations: an offer of ours (an offers: tag from card features, or a pseudo-tag: keyword:<printed keyword>, unit:space, disrupt-resources) answers one threat when its qualifier holds against the archetype: removesKeyUnit checks the parsed cost, HP, power, arena and trait limits (damage must reach printed HP) against each key unit; sweep needs an each/all/any-number effect on enemy units and reachesCheapHp a damage or HP limit at least the median HP of the archetype's cheap units; arena needs the removal to be limited to that arena (or, for a unit offer, the unit to be in it); healsBase needs the heal to reach a base; minPower bounds a unit offer. The weight scales the answer's coverage. Each example is a real card whose clause produces the offer; tests/meta/counters.test.ts checks every one.

threats.title: Key units
threats.reason: Units that at least half of the archetype's decks play; removal that can take them answers the deck's main threats.

threats.title: Upgrade-heavy
threats.reason: Five or more upgrades or Pilots per deck: the deck invests resources in single units, which upgrade removal turns into card advantage.

threats.title: Shield-heavy
threats.reason: Shield tokens blank the first damage each time; upgrade removal and Saboteur strip them.

threats.title: Go-wide
threats.reason: Many token units and units costing 2 or less: one sweeper trades for several cards.

threats.title: Sentinel wall
threats.reason: Eight or more Sentinel units or Sentinel grants per deck stop attacks on the base and on other units; Saboteur attacks past them.

threats.title: Space-heavy
threats.reason: Most of the deck's units fight in space; ground-only removal and ground units do not touch them.

threats.title: Low curve aggro
threats.reason: A mean cost of 3.2 or less races the base early; healing the base buys the turns a slower deck needs.

threats.title: Base pressure
threats.reason: Raid and direct base damage push damage past the board; base healing undoes it.

threats.title: Card-draw engine
threats.reason: The deck plans around drawing and searching for its pieces; discard takes them from hand first.

threats.title: Resource plan
threats.reason: Smuggle, ramp and play-from-resources make the resource row part of the plan; exhausting or defeating resources slows it.

relations.reason: A defeat effect whose cost, HP, arena and trait limits fit the archetype's key units removes them outright.
Direct damage at least the key unit's printed HP defeats it.

example.clause: If you do, deal 5 damage to a unit.

relations.reason: Capturing a key unit removes it until its captor leaves play.

example.clause: Your base captures an enemy non-leader unit.

relations.reason: Returning a key unit to hand costs its owner the tempo and every upgrade on it; it can be replayed, so it counts for less.

example.clause: If you do, return a non-leader unit that costs 4 or less to its owner's hand.

relations.reason: Removing an upgrade undoes the resources and the card spent on it.

example.clause: Defeat a non-leader upgrade attached to a unit.

relations.reason: Shield tokens are upgrades: upgrade removal defeats them, and a Saboteur attacker defeats the defender's Shields before damage.
Damage or defeat on each enemy unit, enough to kill the archetype's typical cheap unit, trades one card for several.

example.clause: Deal 2 damage to each non-Vehicle enemy unit.

relations.reason: Saboteur ignores Sentinel when attacking, so it reaches the base or the unit behind the wall.
Removal aimed at space units, able to take one of the archetype's key space units, is efficient exactly where the archetype fights.

example.clause: Defeat an enemy space unit with 3 or less remaining HP.

relations.reason: A space unit with 4 or more power contests the arena the archetype attacks from.
Healing the base undoes a low curve's early damage and buys the turns to stabilise.

example.clause: If you do, heal 5 damage from a base.

relations.reason: Base healing undoes Raid and direct base damage.
Making the opponent discard takes the drawn or searched piece before it is played.

example.clause: They discard a card from their hand.

relations.reason: Exhausting or defeating enemy resources slows a deck that plays from or counts its resources.
